rawContent: Just before a big storm rolled in on June 2, demonstrators at a police accountability and #BlackLivesMatter rally on the Wisconsin Capitol lawn in Madison talked with @wisconsinlife about why they were there, via @maureenmccollum and @WPR https://t.co/ODgb51FTCs

As @GovEvers states "racism is a public health crisis" and asks the Wisconsin Legislature to address policing policies, @DHSWI warns COVID-19 can still spread beyond local hotspots, including among #BlackLivesMatter protestors, reports @zschultzWPT @PBSWI https://t.co/CsnXt65jrL

The emotion that filled Wisconsin's streets was palpable as demonstrators around the state gathered to declare #BlackLivesMatter after the killing of George Floyd and call for more accountability for law enforcement, reports @willkenneally @PBSWI https://t.co/Ltme5ggvbJ

Why have people across Wisconsin risen up to protest the killing of George Floyd? @fredwistv interviews @blocbyblocMKE director @Angela_Lang about the #BlackLivesMatter movement, fighting white supremacy, and racism as a public health crisis, via @PBSWI https://t.co/l7r0LohbZk

A #BlackLivesMatter march in Wausau was its biggest organized political protest in decades, a measure of how broad the movement against police brutality and racial injustice has grown in Wisconsin's small cities and rural areas, reports @robertmentzer @WPR https://t.co/gw3bDiYwCc

An 11th straight day of #BlackLivesMatter protests in Wisconsin is seeing demonstrations in Madison, Milwaukee and Oconomowoc, following a weekend in which tens of thousands of people marched to decry racism and police violence, reports @WPR https://t.co/KUQAWgfgVf

Many of Wisconsin's professional athletes who play for the @Bucks, @Brewers and @packers have spoken out in support of #BlackLivesMatter protesters across the state as they demonstrate for police accountability, reports @meganmariehart @WPR https://t.co/w4RmgjvXNP

#BlackLivesMatter protests continue to be planned for Milwaukee on June 9 as #wiwx forecasts indicate heavy rains and strong winds across much of Wisconsin into the night, reports @WPR https://t.co/WXCDxRTSqX

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview @TriageUrban founder and CEO Brandi Grayson, an organizer of police accountability demonstrations in Madison, about what protestors demand and the meaning of peace for the #BlackLivesMatter movement, via @PBSWI https://t.co/OwgRRuWDZ4

Artists have transformed the boarded-up windows of storefronts on Madison's State Street, painting murals with messages about George Floyd, #BlackLivesMatter and exhortations of love and power — here are more than a dozen photos of their work, via @PBSWI https://t.co/6YhgPOWXD4

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview @LGMandelaBarnes about the issues local communities face and his vision for Wisconsin's future as #BlackLivesMatter protests over police accountability and racism continue around the state and nation, via @PBSWI https://t.co/lLDupTf3Wa

Nobody is quite sure what will come of the #BlackLivesMatter and police accountability protests, but as artists visit State Street daily to paint murals, Madison is going through a healing process that celebrates Black culture, reports @SJohnsonWPR @WPR https://t.co/GSDLlxQCK6

What role do youth voices have in creating change as the #BlackLivesMatter movement surges? @fredwistv interviews Noah Anderson, a recent @MadisonWestHS graduate who organized students around issues of race, equality and @MMSDschools policy, via @PBSWI https://t.co/jjF1xM9reY

The joint LGBTQ+ rights and #BlackLivesMatter in downtown Madison led by @AboutFreedomInc sought to highlight the role of Black queer people in movements in support of racial justice and Pride, reports @willkenneally @PBSWI https://t.co/HIHTtZRcyK

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview @UW_GndrWomenSt professor @DrSamiSchalk about her research on race, queerness and disability, and her perspective on how LGBTQ communities intersect with the #BlackLivesMatter protests, via @PBSWI https://t.co/5pwKvFJZWA

One focus of #BlackLivesMatter protests in the Milwaukee area is the record of @WauwatosaPD officer Joseph Mensah, who has killed three people while on duty since 2015, with community members calling for his firing and prosecution, reports @CorriHess @WPR https://t.co/vq5hqOuDNV

A growing number of Wisconsinites are showing support for the #BlackLivesMatter movement with their pocketbooks by shopping at Black-owned businesses, though issues like denial of credit and limited access to capital continue, reports @meganmariehart @WPR https://t.co/guGpd2SAWf

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview Christine Neumann-Ortiz, executive director of @voces_milwaukee, about how Wisconsin's Latin American communities intersect with the #BlackLivesMatter movement and efforts against racism and for justice, via @PBSWI https://t.co/DR5oLlEjZ1

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview @UWM_HBSSW professor @DavidJPate and @UWMenglish professor Margaret Noodin about the meaning of #BlackLivesMatter, Indigenous voices and the importance of knowledge embedded in language and places, via @PBSWI https://t.co/qLjoEhfhS0

#BlackLivesMatter protests continue in Milwaukee as groups like @blocbyblocMKE call for changes to policing and more accountability, citing distrust of officers in the wake of practices targeting communities of color, reports @CorriHess @WPR https://t.co/S2A8FGpalp

Sandy Solomon is among a group of around 20 #BlackLivesMatter activists who have marched from Milwaukee to Washington, D.C. to join #NANMOW2020, shares their experiences while on the road against racism and for equality, reports @RachVasquez @wisconsinlife https://t.co/pDf4taXmi6

📺 🖥️ 💻 📱 Watch @marisawojcik interview Khalil Coleman, community activist and The People's Revolution organizer, about the #BlackLivesMatter movement in Milwaukee and how racial justice and police accountability protests are portrayed, via @PBSWI https://t.co/9bIhHuPE07

Barron County is moving to defund Embrace, a domestic violence survivors counseling and advocacy service in northwest Wisconsin, for supporting the #BlackLivesMatter movement and calling for an end to racism and police violence, reports @RichKremer @WPR https://t.co/DAvGKd2WQl

With intense focus on the rhetoric and dynamics of the 2020 presidential campaign, it's unclear how the #BlackLivesMatter movement and ongoing protests for police accountability have affected local elections across Wisconsin, reports @BridgitBowden @WPR https://t.co/MYvihtwYPa

People cited for breaking curfew at #BlackLivesMatter protests in Wauwatosa received a $1,321 ticket — higher than curfew fines of $691 in Milwaukee and $200 in Kenosha — the size of which Mayor Dennis McBride said is under review, reports @CorriHess @WPR https://t.co/DEzLp3VSf1
